newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bahn says infrastructure costs must fall.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bahn says infrastructure costs must fall.

text.p: Deutsche Bahn chairman Heinz Duerr said on Wednesday that the current building costs associated with tracks and other railway infrastructure in Germany are more than double what they should be.
"The construction industry must be creative. Costs have to be reduced by at least 50 percent," Duerr told a lunch organised by the American Chamber of Commerce in Germany.

Duerr cited infrastructure as one of a number of investment challenges facing the German railway in its new status as a shareholding company, with the introduction of information technology systems the other core area.
Deutsche Bahn has a budget of some 77 billion marks up to the year 2000 to eliminate what Duerr called the "enormous investment backlog" resulting from its past as a state-run entity.
An overhaul of its computer systems was needed both to provide better information about its services to customers and to improve links with other transport providers, Duerr said.
He added that research had shown that some 70 percent of Germans never or only rarely used the railway network over a year, partly as a result of its poor marketing.
Duerr said the financial restructuring of the once heavily debt-laden concern that started in the early 1990s still had around eight or 10 years to run.
"It's going to take longer to turn the railways into a really great business than some people think," he said.
